newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 7.

text.p: PRAVO - President Vaclav Havel celebrated his 60th birthday in Prague's Divadlo Archa. Approximately 1,000 guests ranging from politicians to poets were in attendance.

- Prime Minister Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) has fallen behind the Czech Social Democratic Party (CSSD) in popularity polls in September according to the Factum agency. But the current minority coalition government, led by ODS, would acutally increase its standing in the legislative body to a majority of 107 seats from the current 99 if parliamentary elections had been held in September. The far-right Republican Party would not have made the five percent limit needed for seats.
- The President of India will visit the Czech Republic from 11-13 October on an invitation from President Vaclav Havel.
- The Czech National Bank has ended forced administration in Ekoagrobanka Usti nad Labem effective from 27 September. The bank began forced administration on 16 January.
- Sepap sold its daughter company, Sepap Bela pod Bezdezem to P-Obal s.r.o. according to a press spokesman for Sepap. The company's name has been changed to Papirny Bela a.s..
- The volume of foreign currency reserves decreased to $16.552 billion in August, down $23 million from July.
- The state budget for 1997 calls for 18.5 billion crowns to be set aside for regions, with the largest grants, 1.442 billion crowns, going to the city of Prague.
- Teplarny Brno a.s. attained a profit of 179.1 million crowns on turnover of 1.48 billion crowns in 1995. The company has decided to pay a net dividend of 37.5 crowns per share.

- ZPS Zlin a.s. posted sales of 3.4 billion crowns from January to August of this year. Exports made up two billion crowns of those sales. ZPS expects to show gross profits of 270 million crowns on sales of 5.5 billion crowns.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Even though the state budget for 1997 was worked out using different economic forecasts for this year as well as 1997, the Ministry of Finance does not see any need to revise it according to Pavel Stepanek from the ministry.

- Sales of steel plate and shaped iron in the third quarter are expected to the lowest in the history of Vitkovice, according to the company's general manager, Vaclav Pasternak. He blamed the stagnation of Czech industry for the decrease.
- The construction of an industrial waste incinerator in Ceske Budejovice is a good economic and ecological investment according to the general manager of Skoda Plzen, Lubomir Soudek.
- Jan Becher - Karlovarska Becherovka a.s. lost the right to use the Jan Becher trademark in Germany due to a court decision in Munich.
